messages.author: 17c3458e85ecd881
messages.subject: Updating old ggplot2 code - Help!
parts:
Hi All,

I've been trying to re-create some nice graphs that I found online using ggplot2. I assume that the code used by the original developer is now out of date, and I was wondering if somebody could help me update it, so that it stops running into errors. 

I'll outline the data.frame I am calling the plot on:

head(d,10)

             value          Rep time agent
D0-H2O-1  9.659073   1    0   H20
D0-ISO-1  9.925745   2    0   Iso
D1-H2O-1 11.137918   3    1   H20
D1-ISO-1 11.101013   4    1   Iso
D2-H2O-1 10.694017   5    2   H20
D2-ISO-1 10.421580   6    2   Iso
D4-H20-1  8.820280   7    4   H20
D4-ISO-1  9.274550   8    4   Iso
D7-H2O-1  8.757489   9    7   H20
D7-ISO-1  9.287158  10    7   Iso


Below is the code I am using to generate said frame and then plot:

d <- as.data.frame(e[p, ])
colnames(d) <- "value"
d$Rep <- md$Replicate
d$time <- md$Time
d$agent <- md$agent
gg <- ggplot(d, aes(time, value)) + geom_boxplot(aes(factor(time)), 
                                                                               outlier.shape = NA) + theme_bw() + scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(d$time)) + 
                                                       geom_jitter(aes(color = factor(d$agent))) + geom_smooth() + 
                                                       labs(title = paste("1", "2", sep = "/"), x = "time (hours)", y = "RMA value") + scale_color_discrete(name = "treatment")



This seems to work, but does not produce an actual plot. Following this, I tried to call the plot...

> gg
Error: Discrete value supplied to continuous scale

And following this, I attempted to traceback...

>traceback(gg)

8: <environment>
   <environment>
   <environment>
Error in as.vector(x, "character") : 
  cannot coerce type 'environment' to vector of type 'character'


I'm not sure I quite understand the problem or what the error is trying to tell me. Initially, I thought the problem was with the "scale_x_continuous" argument due to the error message, however, removing this argument entirely does nothing to prevent either error from forming.

Any help is greatly appreciated, thanks for your time.
